subject: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — Limitation of Liability framing
messages:
From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@novaanalytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Harrington <tom.harrington@novaanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines (LoL caps and carve-outs)

Karthik —

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team ran a pass and pushed a redline that narrows the liability cap and expands consequential-damage carve-outs. Key asks from Nova: 

- Cap: prefer an annual cap at 1x fees paid in the relevant 12-month period (we proposed 1x annual recurring fees).
- Alternative: a total aggregate cap equal to 2x fees paid over term if Redwood insists on a cumulative approach.
- Carve-outs: broad carve-outs for (i) breaches of confidentiality/security, (ii) IP infringement, and (iii) willful misconduct.
- Consequential damages: remove consequential damages carve-out for data loss in certain regulated workflows — we want limited recovery for real damages.

We attached Nova_Redlines_v3.docx with inline comments. Can you confirm Redwood's position so we can align with procurement and get to signature? We have a Friday legal review deadline.

Thanks,
Samantha Cole
Sr. Contracts Manager
Nova Analytics
Attachment: Nova_Redlines_v3.docx (docx)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@novaanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (LoL caps and carve-outs)

Samantha —

Appreciate the quick pass and clear asks. Looping in Marissa (Commercial Lead) and Laura (Legal) to propose options. High-level: Redwood is open to a structure that balances predictability for Nova with some aggregate protections for Redwood given potential multi-year usage spikes.

Options we'd like your input on (short summary):
1) Annual rolling cap = 1x fees paid in prior 12 months (your ask). Pros: predictable; Cons: potential exposure if usage spikes late in contract term.
2) Aggregate cap = 2x total fees paid to date (Redwood prefers for unlimited burst protection).
3) Hybrid: annual cap for operational incidents, plus a separate per-incident floor for IP/security carve-outs (higher for indemnity events).

Marissa/Laura — can you review Nova's redlines and recommend which option gets executive / pricing approval? If we go with option 1 we may need a modest uplift on unit pricing to offset risk; option 2 may be acceptable with a committed annual minimum.

I will set a 30-min call with Nova if that helps move things faster.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Nova redlines — recommendation and pricing delta

Karthik / Laura —

Quick read and recommendation:
- Legal (Laura): prefer the hybrid approach (option 3). Rationale: preserves customer comfort with an annual cap while limiting Redwood's tail risk for catastrophic events with a separate higher cap/exclusion bucket (IP/security). Also propose carveouts be explicitly limited to "willful misconduct; gross negligence; and obligations to indemnify for third-party IP claims." Avoid language that expands to all "security events" — keep to breaches caused by Redwood.
- Commercial (me): we can accept a 1x rolling annual cap for standard operational failures if Nova agrees to: (a) a 12-month committed minimum spend (AMR), or (b) a 15% uplift on list rates if they remain fully variable. Practical ask: which is easier for Nova — commit or price uplift?

I've sketched numbers in MSA_liability_matrix.xlsx (attachment) showing expected downside exposure by scenario.

Next steps: 1) Karthik to present hybrid language to Nova; 2) Laura to propose precise carveout wording (short paragraph) we can include in next mark; 3) Finance to confirm uplift guardrail — looping Stephanie.

Marissa Cole
VP Revenue
Redwood Inference
Attachment: MSA_liability_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@novaanalytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Harrington <tom.harrington@novaanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (LoL caps and carve-outs)

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick internal review. Nova prefers to avoid committing to a spend floor if possible. The procurement team indicates a price uplift would be acceptable up to ~12% but anything above will push us to look at alternative vendors.

On carveouts: Nova is comfortable with a narrowly tailored IP indemnity and willful misconduct exception but wants security breach recoveries to be recoverable (i.e., not fully carved out) for loss of regulated data. That means we need language that distinguishes (i) Redwood-originating breaches vs (ii) customer misconfiguration or-provider-agnostic causes.

We can do a 30-min call Monday to hash final language if that helps.

Best,
Samantha
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@novaanalytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (LoL caps and carve-outs)

Samantha —

Thanks for the clarity on Nova's position. Per our internal review, Redwood can proceed with the hybrid approach with the following concrete language (we'll insert exact phrasing into the next redline):

1) Liability Cap: "Except for liabilities arising from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence or Redwood's indemnity obligations for third-party claims of intellectual property infringement, the total liability of Redwood under or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, or (ii) $500,000. For clarity, liability relating to Security Incidents shall be addressed in Section X (Security Remedies and Responsibilities)."

2) Security carveout: We will not accept an unlimited cap for security-related damages. Instead we propose a separate security indemnity bucket that preserves customer recovery for verified data breach losses caused by Redwood, subject to remediation offsets and our standard incident response obligations. This keeps recoverability for regulated-data loss but avoids an open-ended exposure.

3) Consequential damages: Continue broad waiver, but exclude enforcement for third-party fines or statutory penalties where applicable (we'll add a limited exception for regulatory fines arising from Redwood's gross negligence).

If Nova accepts the above framing, Redwood requests confirmation on the pricing uplift (12% acceptable to you?) or the commitment alternative (12-month AMR). We will prepare a tracked-redline set for your review.

We can take the Monday 30-min call to finalize if you'd like.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
